name: Autosomal Recessive Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting pelvic and shoulder girdle muscles
Muscle biopsy showing dystrophic changes with absence or reduction of specific sarcoglycan or other associated proteins
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in genes associated with autosomal recessive LGMD

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness with confirmatory muscle biopsy and/or genetic testing identifying biallelic pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic heterogeneity requires comprehensive gene panel testing for accurate diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical proximal muscle weakness of pelvic and shoulder girdles
searchTerms: equal muscle weakness in hips and shoulders
weakness in pelvic and shoulder muscles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle atrophy predominantly in limb-girdle distribution
searchTerms: muscle wasting mainly around hips and shoulders
muscle loss in shoulder and pelvic areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated serum creatine kinase levels (5-10 times normal)
searchTerms: high CK levels indicating muscle damage

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to proximal lower limb weakness
searchTerms: walking difficulty from upper leg weakness
gait problems due to proximal lower limb weakness
difficulty walking from thigh muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Difficulty climbing stairs or rising from a seated position

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness
slight inward curve of lower back

rare.symptomName: Dysphagia due to pharyngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to muscle involvement

imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty replacement and muscle atrophy in proximal limb muscles
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in genes such as SGCA, SGCB, SGCG, SGCD, and others associated with autosomal recessive LGMD
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating dystrophic changes and absence or reduction of sarcoglycan complex proteins

distinguishingFeatures: Facial and scapular muscle involvement early
Genetic testing for D4Z4 repeat contraction

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness over weeks
references: Nigro V, Savarese M. Genetic basis of limb-girdle muscular dystrophies: the 2014 update. Acta Myol. 2014;33(1):1-12.
